content.content:
# 001: Architecture

## Decisions
- **Spotify behind a behaviour.** `Rocola.Spotify` defines the callbacks; `Fake` (default in dev/test)
  and `Web` (real API + `TokenServer`, stub) implement them. Switching is config plus credentials.
  Why: build and test with no account, token or network.
- **Own queue.** Spotify's API can add to its queue but not remove or reorder, so Rocola keeps its
  queue in SQLite (skips, votes, per-guest limits) and feeds Spotify one song ahead.
- **Fake mirrors real limits** (add-only queue, restricted devices, active device required) so
  behaviour proven against it carries over to the real adapter.
- **Stack:** Phoenix LiveView, SQLite (`ecto_sqlite3`), `mix release` for aarch64 on a Raspberry Pi.
- **Tidewave** (dev only) gives the coding agent access to the running app over MCP.

defmodule RocolaWeb.RequestLiveTest do
  use RocolaWeb.ConnCase
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  setup do
    Rocola.Spotify.Fake.reset()
    :ok = Rocola.Spotify.transfer_playback("fake-living-room")
  end

  test "banner updates when the song changes", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, view, html} = live(conn, ~p"/")
    assert html =~ "Nothing playing yet"

    :ok = Rocola.Spotify.add_to_queue("fake:track:0-0")
    send(view.pid, :poll)
    assert render(view) =~ "Midnight Aurora"

    song2 = %{uri: "x", name: "Next Song", artist: "Someone", duration_ms: 1}
    Agent.update(Rocola.Spotify.Fake, &Map.put(&1, :now, song2))
    send(view.pid, :poll)
    html = render(view)
    assert html =~ "Next Song"
    refute html =~ "Midnight Aurora"
  end
end

defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

content.text:
`/` now serves a new `RequestLive` page with a "Now playing" banner. `mix precommit` passes, with 9 tests green.

The banner polls `Rocola.Spotify.now_playing()` every 3 seconds while the page is connected, so it updates when the song changes. I polled because Spotify has no push API and the Fake has no change events. If you'd rather have PubSub, say so; I'd add it once playback goes through `Rocola.Jukebox`.
